evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 12.25 mg/L (46.0h) to 3.69 mg/L (46.2h) and declines to 1.73 mg/L (52.0h), breaching the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Source batches (source-1/2/3) maintained DO2 >=7.4 mg/L through 52h, confirming receiving-only anomaly
Receiving P assays: 0.0 (24h), 0.90 (36h), 2.33 g/L (48h) — production underway and mass retention matters

Forward model: strong_feed_reduction post-decision oxygen_deficit 3.79 mg·h/L, minimum DO 1.16 mg/L, product mass 131.8 kg — best among interventions (keep 1.92/1.24/130.4; combined 6.51/0.99; reduce_feed 8.22/0.87; increase_air 8.20/0.89)
Model sensitivity: strong_feed_reduction min-DO range 0.75–1.77 mg/L, mass range 115.5–183.5 kg — all model variants still violate the constraint
submission.rationale: The receiving batch suffered an abrupt oxygen collapse at ~46h: DO2 fell from ~12.2 mg/L to ~3.7 mg/L in one sample step and continued declining (1.73 mg/L at 52h), already below the 2.0 mg/L operating minimum and trending lower — unlike all three source batches, which stayed well-oxygenated. This is consistent with a sharp rise in oxygen demand relative to transfer capacity late in the batch. Of the bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (feed ×0.6, air ×1.15) directly attacks both sides of the imbalance: it cuts oxygen demand via reduced feed and adds transfer capacity via increased aeration, while retaining product mass (the source-calibrated forward model gives it the highest predicted product mass, ~131.8 kg, and the lowest post-decision oxygen deficit of any intervention). A stop is rejected because it yields zero counted production; weaker single-knob options (reduce_feed or increase_air alone) leave one mechanism unaddressed and the model ranks them worse. Caveat: the forward model is source-calibrated and itself flags a receiving-specific transfer anomaly (estimated multiplier ~0.44), and even the best intervention remains model-infeasible, so the recommendation is the least-violating, mass-preserving correction rather than a guaranteed-feasible one; continuous DO2 monitoring should continue and a stop would remain the fallback if DO cannot be held above 2 mg/L.
submission.uncertainty: High. The physics tool is source-calibrated and its per-action predictions are internally counterintuitive for this receiving batch (e.g., increase_air modeled as worsening DO), so its ranking is only weak evidence. Strong feed reduction risks slowing production; the model's sensitivity spread (product mass 115–183 kg, min DO 0.75–1.77 mg/L) shows no parameter member is feasible. If the true mechanism is an equipment/aeration transfer failure rather than demand overload, only the air-side response helps and feed reduction would sacrifice product unnecessarily; if the mechanism is overfeeding, strong reduction is the correct fix.
